chunk-001:c003.proposition: Explanatory intuitions that operate within material reality need not extend to spacetime or reality as a whole, while a foundational deity could itself exist as a brute rather than necessary fact.

orphanFallback.rationale: Independently of any prior opposing move, the stated limits of totality-level explanatory intuition and the brute-deity alternative directly support the con route's scope objection.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Even if the universe began and is contingent, causal and explanatory intuitions formed within it may not govern its ultimate boundary, leaving the universe's brute existence a live endpoint.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a standalone skeptical argument, the limited reach of within-universe intuitions supplies a reason to treat brute existence at the universe's boundary as plausible.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Calling God's existence necessary does not explain why God exists when necessary existence appears to be a property available only conditional on God's already existing.

orphanFallback.rationale: The conditional ordering between an entity's existence and its alleged necessity independently challenges necessity's capacity to explain that entity's actuality.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Explaining divine necessity through divine supremacy threatens circularity if necessary existence is itself among the properties that make the foundation supreme.

orphanFallback.rationale: The potential reciprocal dependence between supremacy and necessity is a freestanding reason to doubt that supremacy provides a deeper explanation of necessary existence.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Failure to exist in every possible world need not imply dependence, so an ultimate being could be explanatorily independent while existing in only some possible worlds as a brute modal fact.

orphanFallback.rationale: The distinction between explanatory dependence and world-invariant existence independently blocks an inference from ultimacy or independence to modal necessity.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: Logical principles may govern statements and inference rather than constitute an ontological structure embedded in reality, because contradictions characterize claims rather than concrete objects such as rocks or clocks.

orphanFallback.rationale: The linguistic or inferential interpretation of logic independently raises the abstract-to-concrete bridge problem without presupposing any earlier opposing claim.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: Although denial-generated contradiction can explain the necessity of abstract truths such as arithmetic, no analogous fact has been identified that makes a concrete being such as God unable not to exist.

orphanFallback.rationale: The contrast between intelligible abstract necessity and unsupported concrete necessity independently establishes a burden to bridge logical truths to a concrete necessary being.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: A brute or unexplained foundation need not exist in every possible world, so moving from explanatory fundamentality to necessary existence is unwarranted.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently distinguishes having no further explanation from existing in every possible world and therefore directly supports the con-side modal objection.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: Necessary existence supplies no genuine explanation of why God exists, while comparable unexplained bruteness can instead be assigned to the universe.

orphanFallback.rationale: Even without an earlier opposing move, the parity between a brute deity and a brute universe challenges the claimed discriminatory advantage of a necessary foundation.
